attempted_claim: Let T* be the once-punctured torus and let F_n(T*) be its ordered configuration space over Q. For n >= 3 let W_n be the FIM+-module of new secondary generators in H_n(F_{2n-2}(T*); Q) with secondary stabilization adding an orbiting pair of points near the puncture, where Wawrykow proved W is neither free nor stably zero and is generated by classes supported on at most 4 points. Decide whether the exact secondary generation degree of W is 4, i.e. whether some class in H_4(F_6(T*); Q) — strictly below the primary-stability onset n >= 9 for H_4 — lies outside the combined span of the primary FI-image from H_4(F_5(T*)) and the secondary orbiting-pair images of classes supported on at most 3 points, so that a 4-point secondary generator is required. A complete answer proves generation of W by classes on at most 3 points with an explicit secondary bound, or exhibits a specific 4-point secondary-unstable class in H_4(F_6(T*)) not in that combined span.
decisive_failure: No verified chain-level secondary stabilization map for the punctured torus was established; the candidate finite-field Kriz model mismatched known Betti numbers at n=4 (30 vs 38); n=5,6 FI-quotients and the H_4(F_6) rank certificate were never reached; conclusions stop at the documented blocking obstacle.
